title: Arithmetic theories: Robinson arithmetic, induction, and nonstandard models
summary: Compare Robinson arithmetic with Peano induction, and use compactness to obtain arithmetic models with elements outside the standard copy.
abstract: Can first-order axioms distinguish the natural numbers from every other arithmetic structure? Robinson arithmetic describes zero, successor, addition and multiplication well enough to get every calculation on numerals right, yet permits an extra element that is its own successor. Peano arithmetic adds induction for every first-order formula, with parameters, and excludes that example. Compactness nevertheless produces a model with elements unequal to every numeral, even if we require every sentence true in the usual natural numbers. These models do not violate induction: its instances govern definable subsets, while the copy of the usual natural numbers inside a nonstandard model cannot be defined, even with parameters.
